https://www.tribtoday.com/news/local-new.text: News Local News Latest News Obituaries Business Community News Police Blotters Ohio News National News International News Sports Local Sports Sport columns High School Sports YSU Sports Ohio Sports National Sports Opinion Guest Columnists Editorials Letters to the Editor Life Lifestyles Ticket Society Burton Cole column Deals on Wheels Classifieds Garage Sales Jobs Contact Information Contact Us Advertise Subscribe Statement of Values Terms of Service Submit News Public Notices Browse notices Place a notice Facebook Twitter Local News Howland OKs support for water trail extension By BRANDON CANTWELL August 13, 2026 2 min read Trending HOWLAND -- The Mahoning River has been a central focus in the area for the past few years at both the state and local level, and Howland trustees at Wednesday's meeting approved a resolution aimed at helping to promote its growth. Trustees approved providing a resolution of support for an application proposing to extend the Mahoning River Water Trail. The resolution states that Howland will join other entities such as Girard, Weathersfield, McDonald, Youngstown, Campbell, Struthers, Lowellville and Poland, as well as the Mahoning River Corridor Initiative and Mahoning River Corridor Mayors Association to extend it, to encourage tourism and eco-friendly, educational, historical, cultural and recreational activities on the river. The resolution, a version of which Girard officials passed at the city council meeting Monday, acknowledges that Howland fronts on the Mahoning River and is traversed by Mosquito Creek, one of the river's main tributaries, which provides "significant opportunities" for water-based recreation, wildlife observation and environmental education and conservation. The resolution states the participating communities recognize the long-term vision of extending the regional water trail network, by developing a future Mosquito Creek Water Trail from the dam to its meeting point with the Mahoning River. The new water trail is expected to enhance regional connectivity, public access, outdoor recreation and the Mahoning River's stewardship. Planning Director Kim Mascarella said the water trail will be extended all the way down through Lowellville. "There have been extensive upgrades to parks along the river, dredging of certain parts of the river, the removal of dams," Mascarella said. "That greatly enhances recreational opportunities all along the Mahoning River, and Mosquito Creek drains into the Mahoning River in the front, near Bolindale." Mascarella said the trail will extend from just Trumbull to both Trumbull and Mahoning counties, but she wasn't sure of its total acreage or linear mileage. Starting at /week. Subscribe Today

https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/videos/cmy83w.text: Emotional reunions with loved ones for Oleshky evacuees Emotional reunions with loved ones for Oleshky evacuees Close People evacuated from the devastated Russian-occupied city of Oleshky were reunited with their loved ones after crossing from Belarus into Ukraine on Saturday. This comes as a ceasefire brokered by US First Lady Melania Trump took effect across the frontline region of Kherson on Tuesday. Families were reunited at a site in the region of Chernihiv in northern Ukraine after arriving in buses and ambulances. They had previously travelled via Crimea and Russia after their evacuation from the Ukrainian town on Friday. Ceasefire measures will remain in place until the end of Sunday 1 November. The BBC's Dan Johnson reports from the site in the Chernihiv region, near the northern Ukrainian border with Belarus. Read more on this story. https://www.monitor.co.me/trumps-america.text: foto: NATO Share Tweet Some key NATO members were not invited to a meeting of the alliance in Poland on October 6. Among them are France, Great Britain, and the Baltic states. The view held by Elbridge Colby—the Under Secretary of war for Policy —is that NATO states which have not aligned their policies with Washington’s priorities should not be considered reliable allies. On October 6, a gathering of NATO members started in Poland. The main event is the discussion of of the future development of the alliance, which is to be followed by two expert conferences, one of them on NATO infrastructure. However, not all the member-states will get an opportunity on the NATO strategy and, means of its implementation. Some of them were not invited. Among them France and Great Britain, which possess nuclear weapons, as well as the Baltic states, on which territory American troops are deployed as a part of the Eastern NATO’s flank joint defense. It was the idea of Under Secretary of war for Elbridge Colby to deal with members of NATO depending on their willingness to comply with the approach of the US administration. The governments that have not aligned their policy with the priorities of Washington should not be regarded as trusted allies. Those that are `meeting American demands should be included in the inner circle and their opinion should be counted. Colby, who has been allowed to carry out his initiative, held a first meeting with the six most favored NATO allies Bergen, Norway, in June. The Bergen Group formed at this meeting includes Norway, Sweden, Finland, Poland, Germany and the Netherlands. Now, the US administration is considering adding Denmark to the exclusive club. It was invited to the current meeting, but might participate in the next one. The NATO countries involved in the Bergen format insist that its existence is not going to rupture the alliance. They pretend to believe that the group intends to come up with ideas it will be bought to the full alliance for further discussion. There is little doubt that the US administration just does not need that. Of course Washington has no intention to withdraw the US from NATO, despite the threats of president Donald Trump during his first term. The US forces depend on NATO infrastructure, which, as the war against Iran has shown, can be used in accordance with the US plans, even if they are not supported by the most of the NATO states. Ramstein air base located in Germany aqone hosts more than twenty thousand US military aircraft movements per year. No substitute can be found. The US also depends on NATO intelligence and early warning capabilities distributed across Europe and the North Atlantic. Colby, who is in charge of the US defense strategy has noted recently that the main task of NATO is to give Europe more military capacity. Europe should be able to defend itself in order to diminish the necessity of the US military presence and the risk of the war between Russia and the EU countries. Besides, Colby also insists on reviving Germany as a military power to contain Russia. If it can be achieved, the US administration will be able to get two advantages out of it. First, Germany will lose prospects of reemerging as the main importer and distributor of Russian oil and gas in Europe. Second, in that case, the US relations with Germany and Russia will be better than their mutual connections. Therefore, the US administration will be act as a mediator and manage the confrontation. Thanks to that, Washington will retain political control over Europe, without increasing expenditures on American military presence or involvement in European defense. It will the US an opportunity to focus its efforts on contend with China’s rise, which the incumbent US administration regards as the main geopolitical challenge. According to Colby’s vision shared by the whole Trump’s administration, the allies, which adhere to Washington’s wishes, should be able to count on American protection, and those that do not support U.S. interests should suffer consequences. There is no need to discuss NATO’s future with those who cannot be used in the American interests or does not want to be useful for the US. A similar approach is used to all American allies, not only the NATO’s states. In August, Trump abruptly ordered to downsize annual joint military exercise with South Korea, because of its refusal to join the war against Iran. The main most important feature of the imperial ideology is the belief that national security must rest on relations of domination. That’s why Trump officially revived the Monroe Doctrine and wants to reassert the US dominance in the Western Hemisphere. On September 21, a day before his speech at the UN General Assembly, Trump published a picture in his Truth Social network, in which he looks at the Western Hemisphere on the globe. The picture is signed “His Hemisphere”. This publication provoked such fierce reaction that the US president found it necessary to repeat the publication in several days to show that the international outcry had no impact on him. President of Brazil Lula da Silva, who spoke just ahead of Trump, stated that “renewed hegemonic temptations” pose a threat to Latin America and the Caribbean. He added that “Brazil does not fit in anyone’s backyard” and needs “partners with a positive agenda that fosters development”, implying that China’s offers look preferable. The results of the first round of Brazilian elections held on October 4, showed that approach of Lula da Silva to the relations with US is not supported by the majority of the Brazilian society. The main Trump’s opponent in the region was surpassed by Flavio Bolsonaro, a son of the former president. The vote margin between two main rivals is quite narrow, Bolsonaro received 47% of votes and Lula 45%. Therefore, the president still has a good chance to win in the second round. However, it should be taken into consideration that Flavio Bolsonaro can be regarded to a certain degree as a substitute to his father, Jair Bolsonaro, who was an ally of the US and remains a close friend of the incumbent American president. In July 2025, Trump even imposed 50% tariffs on Brazilian goods to make Lula stop prosecution of Jair Bolsonaro, who is still under a house arrest. But if he had been allowed to participate in the election, he could have been more successful than his son. So even in Brazil the idea of the US dominance in the Western Hemisphere is not generally rejected, to say the least. And Trump’s ambition to turn the US into empire that dominates on the global level cannot be fulfilled without securing that natural resources and trade routes in Latin America are controlled solely by the US. As a result, Europe is not going to be in the main focus of the US foreign policy in the near future. A few days before the beginning of the NATO meeting in Poland, the Trump’s administration made a symbolic gesture to demonstrate it. Washington redirected tens of millions of dollars approved previously as military assistance for Slovakia and North Macedonia to Latin America. The same happened with the funds designated for the support of the Iraqi forces. They were also diverted to Latin America, though on September 30, the last American troops left Iraq, ending 23 years of US military presence. Meanwhile, Shia militias, which are defying government control, have not been disarmed. Iraqi government turned out to be incapable of doing it, despite pledges of prime minister Ali al-Zaidi. Now, Baghdad is going to depend on Tehran’s assistance in restraining Shia armed groups. The US funds allotted for the military assistance to Iraq were insufficient to make Shia militias relinquish weapons, but taking the money away the Trump’s administration wanted to demonstrate its complete unconcern about it. The failure in the war with Iran made it impossible for the US administration to increase control over the Middle East. Due to that, Washington sees no reason to spend effort on supporting American allies in the region, even if it means that Iran will get an opportunity to increase its influence. Donald Trump has also made clear that he has no intention to abandon a ceasefire the US reached with Houthis last year, after Yemen’s Shia armed movement captured captured strategic islands and coastal towns and disrupted Saudi oil export through Bab-el-mandeb Strait. The next US administration, even if it will be a Republican one, might not so easily withdraw from its commitments with the US allies as the current one. However, Europe and the Middle East will remain less important for the US than Latin America and East Asia. Europe is losing its geopolitical and economic significance on the global level, maybe, for the first time in five hundred years. It has been caused by emerging other centers of global development, first of all in China, which are becoming European rivals. Besides, during “cold war” Europe was the main arena of confrontation between the US and the USSR. After the American victory, the US required assistance of its European allies in the globalization process, which was regarded as the way to strengthen Western dominance. However, the globalization has reached its limits without achieving this goal. Moreover, the US has to put more effort into retaining a leading position in the global political system. So the European countries cannot count on the strong American support any more. Of course, Trump’s inability to recognize importance of the transatlantic partnership undermines both European and American influence in the world. However, a historic crisis relations between the US and the EU caused not only by the approach of the Trump’s administration, but also by objective reasons. They can be overcome, only if the EU helps Europe to regain its global significance. First, through technological leadership in the spheres that have the strongest impact on the geopolitical situation. Trump believes that the US will secure its global dominance, if it wins the race against China in the development of AI systems. The US is commanding approximately 50% of worldwide AI compute power and producing the highest number of notable frontier AI models. China is trying to compete with the US for global influence by focusing on cost-efficient open-source models and hardware manufacturing. The only EU country that has a notable influence on the development of the AI systems is France. And in the other spheres that affect the international development, for instance in industrial robot deployments, situation is not much better. Second, through defending and spreading worldwide the values on which the EU is claimed to be grounded. The outcome of elections in the Republika Srpska have shown once again the EU has failed this task even in the neighboring countries. If Europe becomes less important on the global level, the EU will inevitably lose some of its social achievements and economic prosperity. However, there have still been no notable attempts to reverse dangerous tendencies. In a speech before the UN General Assembly, he told Iranian leaders to understand that he is “not running for office” and that the potential outcome of the U.S. Elections cannot influence his approach to the war On October 20, it was reported that Elon Musk ordered a slowdown of Starshield (a military-grade satellite network built by SpaceX) services in Ukraine. Musk himself had earlier denied giving any direct orders. However, it is easy to comprehend the reasons both for his decision to slowdown Starshield, and for attempts to evade responsibility for it. Like many people, who got involved in politics, but have no political talents, he understands others too literally and too easily gets confused, when his mistakes are found out. The US president Donald Trump did not want Ukraine to lose ability to conduct air-attacks in the depths of Russian territory. He just wanted to show that he was annoyed with Ukraine and justify his intentions to start economic cooperation with Russia before establishing truce. Trump does not need Russian problems to be solved before the agreement with the Kremlin is reached. In accordance with his intentions, Ukraine should not be defeated, but it should be in a difficult situation and unable to find a way out of it by itself. Musk can be advised to take an example from Pete Hegseth, the US secretary of war, who did not forbid to supply Ukraine with missiles for “Patriot” air defense systems. He is not just giving permission to do it. At present, Trump does not need peaceful solutions both in Iran and Ukraine, because after his failure in the war with Iran, he wants to work out a new strategy first. And it, in its turn, will depend on his agreement with China. Until it is reached, he is interested to keep both conflicts in their current state. Any efforts to make him take a decision will prove to be fruitless. On October 16, Russian president Vladimir Putin chaired a meeting with senior members of the General staff of the Russian armed forces. It should be noted that after the famous American public relations firm Ketchum terminated its contract for managing the Kremlin’s image in 2015, the organization of the events with Putin’s participation has been gradually deteriorating. The meeting purposed to persuade everyone that Russia is very close to victory, was held under the camouflage net, but inside the building. Such design was surely supposed to create impression that the leaders of the successful army are commanding its offensive operations close to the battlefield. It just looked comically. However, even if the meeting had more persuasive appearance, it would not influence Trump’s position. He is not trying to help the Kremlin to end the war on its terms. He just showed that he would be willing to do it, if he found it useful. There were forecasts that special envoys of the US president Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner would demand capitulation from Ukrainian president Volodymir Zelenskyy at the negotiations in Oslo, on October 20. Those dark predictions proved to be wrong. Witkoff and Kushner came to discuss the potential peace frameworks and confirm that the US resume sharing early-warning data on Russian missile attacks. Trump’s approach to the resolution of the war with Iran is the same. He has nothing against it, he just does not need it now. The American president at his speech at the UN General assembly warned Iranian leaders that they were making a mistake thinking that he would need a peace treaty to improve the results of the Republican party on the Congress midterm elections. He advised them to realize that “he is not running” and the possible outcome of elections cannot influence his approach to the war. The US president might exaggerate his indifference to the election
